For every keyboard, applyConfigToKeyboard reads six keymap names per device (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1213-1238, applyConfigToKeyboard): for example the kb_layout lookup asks the device first and the global option second (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1226-1231, kb_layout and its siblings). The block exists when one carries the keyboard's exact normalised name (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1196-1201, deviceConfigExists; the name is the `name` the dump prints), and the STRVAL_EMPTY sentinel reads as the empty string (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1156-1168, STRVAL_EMPTY; its spelling `[[EMPTY]]` lives in a Hyprland header outside these pins). The global defaults are `us` for the layout and empty for the rest (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:271-276, default XKB names). When nothing changed since the last apply, the keyboard is skipped (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1270-1280, did not change). .ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-junk-full/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 5. What the dump shows. `hyprctl devices -j` prints the stored rules of each keyboard - rules, model, layout, variant, options - and for each pointer a `scrollFactor` with two decimals (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:765-772, scrollFactor field; Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:785-802, layout and the other stored names). The keyboard object also carries `active_keymap` and `active_layout_index` (the compiled keymap's active layout, named in XKB's words such as `Portuguese (Brazil)`, not the config's `br`), `capsLock` and `numLock` (locked-modifier state, not the `numlock_by_default` option) and `main` (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:793-801, main and the lock fields), which marks the keyboard `switchxkblayout main` acts on, not the primary hardware keyboard: on this host only the input-method virtual keyboard has it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1934-1942, disableAllKeyboards clears main for physical keyboards). The `mice` list holds every pointer, touchpads included, and its `defaultSpeed` is libinput's default, not the configured sensitivity. A pointer's factor is the device block's `scroll_factor` clamped to 0..100 only when that block explicitly sets it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1376-1383, scroll_factor explicitly set), and is otherwise unset, printed as -1.00 (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1379-1383, nullopt branch). The global `input:scroll_factor` (range 0..2, unlike the block's 0..100 clamp) never reaches the printed field (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:290-300, input:scroll_factor is a separate global option), and neither does `input:touchpad:scroll_factor`.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-junk-full/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:35 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 6. Virtual keyboards. A virtual keyboard (an input method such as fcitx5) is named `hl-virtual-keyboard`, followed, while `misc:name_vk_after_proc` is on (the default), by `-` and the normalised name of its client's binary or `-unknown` (<redacted-shape>.cpp:11-31, hl-virtual-keyboard naming). The config's names are applied to it once at creation; when its client sends a keymap the keyboard marks the keymap overridden (Hyprland-VirtualKeyboard.cpp:36-44, virtual keyboard override flag), and setKeymap then returns early (Hyprland-IKeyboard.cpp:60-64, keymap overridden early return), so the rules the dump prints for it are the creation-time names, not a witness of the keymap in use; its `active_keymap` does name the active layout of the client's keymap.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-junk-full/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:36 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 7. Names. A device's name is lower-cased with space, newline and comma replaced by `-` (Hyprland-MiscFunctions.cpp:777-789, lower-case name normalizer), an empty result becomes `unknown-device`, and a name already taken by any input device gets a `-1`, `-2` suffix (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:2119-2131, duplicate suffix). A block written with the product name as the kernel reports it (`Razer DeathAdder V2`) never matches: the lookup compares the stored key exactly. The wiki tells the user to copy the name from `hyprctl devices` (wiki-Keywords.md:79, hyprctl devices names) and documents that per-device options overwrite the `input` ones (wiki-Keywords.md:64-70, wiki override rule).

List lines. `read_config_paths` reads every list file immediately, in the order of step 1, rather than on demand (`All config files are read immediatelly, rather than on demand, even if it's more IO intensive`, xdg-terminal-exec:353) and pins the locale to `C` by re-invoking itself (xdg-terminal-exec:355-358). Which one wins when both exist was not in the receipt; the round-48 w2 reproduction placed differing files at both and `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/xkb` won (`.ufo/waves/round-48/w2/CritC2FalseClaim/probe.txt:264`), as the order above predicts.

.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-junk-no-registry/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:23 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl | what `hyprctl devices -j` prints for a keyboard and a mouse | step 5 | sourced |
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-junk-no-registry/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:32 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 3. Per-keyboard lookup. For every keyboard, applyConfigToKeyboard reads six keymap names per device (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1213-1238, applyConfigToKeyboard): for example the kb_layout lookup asks the device first and the global option second (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1226-1231, kb_layout and its siblings). The device value counts only when the user set it; otherwise the global fallback applies (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1115-1123, set-by-user test then global fallback). The block exists when one carries the keyboard's exact normalised name (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1196-1201, deviceConfigExists; the name is the `name` the dump prints), and the STRVAL_EMPTY sentinel reads as the empty string (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1156-1168, STRVAL_EMPTY; its spelling `[[EMPTY]]` lives in a Hyprland header outside these pins). The global defaults are `us` for the layout and empty for the rest (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:271-276, default XKB names). When nothing changed since the last apply, the keyboard is skipped (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1270-1280, did not change). Every `input:kb_*` option re-applies input devices when changed, which is how a runtime `hyprctl keyword` reaches a keyboard.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-junk-no-registry/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 5. What the dump shows. `hyprctl devices -j` prints the stored rules of each keyboard - rules, model, layout, variant, options - and for each pointer a `scrollFactor` with two decimals (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:765-772, scrollFactor field; Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:785-802, layout and the other stored names). The keyboard object also carries `active_keymap` and `active_layout_index` (the compiled keymap's active layout, named in XKB's words such as `Portuguese (Brazil)`, not the config's `br`), `capsLock` and `numLock` (locked-modifier state, not the `numlock_by_default` option) and `main` (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:793-801, main and the lock fields), which marks the keyboard `switchxkblayout main` acts on, not the primary hardware keyboard: on this host only the input-method virtual keyboard has it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1934-1942, disableAllKeyboards clears main for physical keyboards). The `mice` list holds every pointer, touchpads included, and its `defaultSpeed` is libinput's default, not the configured sensitivity. A pointer's factor is the device block's `scroll_factor` clamped to 0..100 only when that block explicitly sets it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1376-1383, scroll_factor explicitly set), and is otherwise unset, printed as -1.00 (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1379-1383, nullopt branch). The global `input:scroll_factor` (range 0..2, unlike the block's 0..100 clamp) never reaches the printed field (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:290-300, input:scroll_factor is a separate global option), and neither does `input:touchpad:scroll_factor`.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-junk-no-registry/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:35 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 6. Virtual keyboards. A virtual keyboard (an input method such as fcitx5) is named `hl-virtual-keyboard`, followed, while `misc:name_vk_after_proc` is on (the default), by `-` and the normalised name of its client's binary or `-unknown` (<redacted-shape>.cpp:11-31, hl-virtual-keyboard naming). The config's names are applied to it once at creation; when its client sends a keymap the keyboard marks the keymap overridden (Hyprland-VirtualKeyboard.cpp:36-44, virtual keyboard override flag), and setKeymap then returns early (Hyprland-IKeyboard.cpp:60-64, keymap overridden early return), so the rules the dump prints for it are the creation-time names, not a witness of the keymap in use; its `active_keymap` does name the active layout of the client's keymap.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-junk-no-registry/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:36 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 7. Names. A device's name is lower-cased with space, newline and comma replaced by `-` (Hyprland-MiscFunctions.cpp:777-789, lower-case name normalizer), an empty result becomes `unknown-device`, and a name already taken by any input device gets a `-1`, `-2` suffix (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:2119-2131, duplicate suffix). A block written with the product name as the kernel reports it (`Razer DeathAdder V2`) never matches: the lookup compares the stored key exactly. The wiki tells the user to copy the name from `hyprctl devices` (wiki-Keywords.md:79, hyprctl devices names) and documents that per-device options overwrite the `input` ones (wiki-Keywords.md:64-70, wiki override rule).

.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-junk-no-registry/corpus/knowledge/xdg-terminal-selection-r47.md:33 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] config 1. Lists and their order. `make_paths` builds two ordered lists and one path. `IFS=':'` (xdg-terminal-exec:145) then the config sequence (xdg-terminal-exec:148-163): for each of `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}` and `${XDG_CONFIG_DIRS:-/etc/xdg}`, first every lowercased `$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` item as `${dir}/${desktop}-xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:150-152, the lowercasing done once with `tr` at xdg-terminal-exec:1144), then `${dir}/xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:153); after both config dirs, the same pair per `${XDG_DATA_DIRS:-/usr/local/share:/usr/share}` inside an `xdg-terminal-exec/` subdir (xdg-terminal-exec:157-163). The result `XTE__CONFIGS` is read left to right as *decreasing* preference, so the two system entries come last - which is what makes an `/execarg_default` line in the distro list (step 2) a low-priority default. The applications list (xdg-terminal-exec:166-169) is built the other way round, each new `${dir}/applications` prepended to the front (`XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS=${xte__dir%/}/applications/${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS:+:${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS}}`, xdg-terminal-exec:168), so it ends up in *ascending* preference - lowest-priority data dir first. The cache file is `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/xdg-terminal-exec` (xdg-terminal-exec:172-173).
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-junk-no-registry/corpus/knowledge/xdg-terminal-selection-r47.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 2. List lines. `read_config_paths` reads every list file immediately, in the order of step 1, rather than on demand (`All config files are read immediatelly, rather than on demand, even if it's more IO intensive`, xdg-terminal-exec:353) and pins the locale to `C` by re-invoking itself (xdg-terminal-exec:355-358). A missing file is not an error (xdg-terminal-exec:365). Each line is trimmed by `read -r` and matched by `case`: the five directives `/enable_cache`, `/disable_cache`, `/execarg_compat`, `/execarg_strict` and `/execarg_default:<id>:<arg>` (xdg-terminal-exec:374-421), of which the first two and the first two of the second pair honour only *the first encountered* occurrence via their `*_CONFIGURED` guards (xdg-terminal-exec:376-379); then the entry-ID form `[a-zA-Z0-9_]* | [+-][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)` (xdg-terminal-exec:425). A leading `+` or `-` is cut off as an exclusion marker (xdg-terminal-exec:427-437): `-id` appends to `XTE__EXCLUDED_ENTRY_IDS` (xdg-terminal-exec:462) and `+id` protects an id only from a *later* `-id` (the first of the pair wins; an earlier exclusion stands, fixture `<redacted-shape>`), each list refusing duplicates. Only the first `:` splits the line, ID from action ID (xdg-terminal-exec:435-438); both halves must validate (xdg-terminal-exec:439) or the line is discarded with a message (xdg-terminal-exec:467). A plain line is appended to `XTE__ENTRY_IDS` in file order, which is the explicit preference order (xdg-terminal-exec:442). Comments and empty lines match no arm and are ignored.

.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-placeholder-full/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:32 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 3. Per-keyboard lookup. For every keyboard, applyConfigToKeyboard reads six keymap names per device (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1213-1238, applyConfigToKeyboard): for example the kb_layout lookup asks the device first and the global option second (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1226-1231, kb_layout and its siblings). The device value counts only when the user set it; otherwise the global fallback applies (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1115-1123, set-by-user test then global fallback). The block exists when one carries the keyboard's exact normalised name (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1196-1201, deviceConfigExists; the name is the `name` the dump prints), and the STRVAL_EMPTY sentinel reads as the empty string (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1156-1168, STRVAL_EMPTY; its spelling `[[EMPTY]]` lives in a Hyprland header outside these pins). The global defaults are `us` for the layout and empty for the rest (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:271-276, default XKB names). When nothing changed since the last apply, the keyboard is skipped (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1270-1280, did not change). Every `input:kb_*` option re-applies input devices when changed, which is how a runtime `hyprctl keyword` reaches a keyboard.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-placeholder-full/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 5. What the dump shows. `hyprctl devices -j` prints the stored rules of each keyboard - rules, model, layout, variant, options - and for each pointer a `scrollFactor` with two decimals (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:765-772, scrollFactor field; Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:785-802, layout and the other stored names). The keyboard object also carries `active_keymap` and `active_layout_index` (the compiled keymap's active layout, named in XKB's words such as `Portuguese (Brazil)`, not the config's `br`), `capsLock` and `numLock` (locked-modifier state, not the `numlock_by_default` option) and `main` (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:793-801, main and the lock fields), which marks the keyboard `switchxkblayout main` acts on, not the primary hardware keyboard: on this host only the input-method virtual keyboard has it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1934-1942, disableAllKeyboards clears main for physical keyboards). The `mice` list holds every pointer, touchpads included, and its `defaultSpeed` is libinput's default, not the configured sensitivity. A pointer's factor is the device block's `scroll_factor` clamped to 0..100 only when that block explicitly sets it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1376-1383, scroll_factor explicitly set), and is otherwise unset, printed as -1.00 (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1379-1383, nullopt branch). The global `input:scroll_factor` (range 0..2, unlike the block's 0..100 clamp) never reaches the printed field (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:290-300, input:scroll_factor is a separate global option), and neither does `input:touchpad:scroll_factor`.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-placeholder-full/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:35 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 6. Virtual keyboards. A virtual keyboard (an input method such as fcitx5) is named `hl-virtual-keyboard`, followed, while `misc:name_vk_after_proc` is on (the default), by `-` and the normalised name of its client's binary or `-unknown` (<redacted-shape>.cpp:11-31, hl-virtual-keyboard naming). The config's names are applied to it once at creation; when its client sends a keymap the keyboard marks the keymap overridden (Hyprland-VirtualKeyboard.cpp:36-44, virtual keyboard override flag), and setKeymap then returns early (Hyprland-IKeyboard.cpp:60-64, keymap overridden early return), so the rules the dump prints for it are the creation-time names, not a witness of the keymap in use; its `active_keymap` does name the active layout of the client's keymap.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-placeholder-full/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:36 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 7. Names. A device's name is lower-cased with space, newline and comma replaced by `-` (Hyprland-MiscFunctions.cpp:777-789, lower-case name normalizer), an empty result becomes `unknown-device`, and a name already taken by any input device gets a `-1`, `-2` suffix (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:2119-2131, duplicate suffix). A block written with the product name as the kernel reports it (`Razer DeathAdder V2`) never matches: the lookup compares the stored key exactly. The wiki tells the user to copy the name from `hyprctl devices` (wiki-Keywords.md:79, hyprctl devices names) and documents that per-device options overwrite the `input` ones (wiki-Keywords.md:64-70, wiki override rule).

.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-placeholder-full/corpus/knowledge/xdg-terminal-selection-r47.md:33 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] config 1. Lists and their order. `make_paths` builds two ordered lists and one path. `IFS=':'` (xdg-terminal-exec:145) then the config sequence (xdg-terminal-exec:148-163): for each of `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}` and `${XDG_CONFIG_DIRS:-/etc/xdg}`, first every lowercased `$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` item as `${dir}/${desktop}-xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:150-152, the lowercasing done once with `tr` at xdg-terminal-exec:1144), then `${dir}/xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:153); after both config dirs, the same pair per `${XDG_DATA_DIRS:-/usr/local/share:/usr/share}` inside an `xdg-terminal-exec/` subdir (xdg-terminal-exec:157-163). The result `XTE__CONFIGS` is read left to right as *decreasing* preference, so the two system entries come last - which is what makes an `/execarg_default` line in the distro list (step 2) a low-priority default. The applications list (xdg-terminal-exec:166-169) is built the other way round, each new `${dir}/applications` prepended to the front (`XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS=${xte__dir%/}/applications/${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS:+:${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS}}`, xdg-terminal-exec:168), so it ends up in *ascending* preference - lowest-priority data dir first. The cache file is `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/xdg-terminal-exec` (xdg-terminal-exec:172-173).
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c1-placeholder-full/corpus/knowledge/xdg-terminal-selection-r47.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 2. List lines. `read_config_paths` reads every list file immediately, in the order of step 1, rather than on demand (`All config files are read immediatelly, rather than on demand, even if it's more IO intensive`, xdg-terminal-exec:353) and pins the locale to `C` by re-invoking itself (xdg-terminal-exec:355-358). A missing file is not an error (xdg-terminal-exec:365). Each line is trimmed by `read -r` and matched by `case`: the five directives `/enable_cache`, `/disable_cache`, `/execarg_compat`, `/execarg_strict` and `/execarg_default:<id>:<arg>` (xdg-terminal-exec:374-421), of which the first two and the first two of the second pair honour only *the first encountered* occurrence via their `*_CONFIGURED` guards (xdg-terminal-exec:376-379); then the entry-ID form `[a-zA-Z0-9_]* | [+-][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)` (xdg-terminal-exec:425). A leading `+` or `-` is cut off as an exclusion marker (xdg-terminal-exec:427-437): `-id` appends to `XTE__EXCLUDED_ENTRY_IDS` (xdg-terminal-exec:462) and `+id` protects an id only from a *later* `-id` (the first of the pair wins; an earlier exclusion stands, fixture `<redacted-shape>`), each list refusing duplicates. Only the first `:` splits the line, ID from action ID (xdg-terminal-exec:435-438); both halves must validate (xdg-terminal-exec:439) or the line is discarded with a message (xdg-terminal-exec:467). A plain line is appended to `XTE__ENTRY_IDS` in file order, which is the explicit preference order (xdg-terminal-exec:442). Comments and empty lines match no arm and are ignored.

Each user path is live: a five-line `symbols/zz` placed at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/xkb` or at `$HOME/.xkb` makes the otherwise fatal `zz` compile (rc 0), and without either path the same run fails XKB-338 (the receipt carries this as a recipe with expected rc, not as captured output). .ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-in-cell-per-row/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:32 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 3. Per-keyboard lookup. For every keyboard, applyConfigToKeyboard reads six keymap names per device (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1213-1238, applyConfigToKeyboard): for example the kb_layout lookup asks the device first and the global option second (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1226-1231, kb_layout and its siblings). The device value counts only when the user set it; otherwise the global fallback applies (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1115-1123, set-by-user test then global fallback). The block exists when one carries the keyboard's exact normalised name (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1196-1201, deviceConfigExists; the name is the `name` the dump prints), and the STRVAL_EMPTY sentinel reads as the empty string (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1156-1168, STRVAL_EMPTY; its spelling `[[EMPTY]]` lives in a Hyprland header outside these pins). The global defaults are `us` for the layout and empty for the rest (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:271-276, default XKB names). When nothing changed since the last apply, the keyboard is skipped (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1270-1280, did not change). Every `input:kb_*` option re-applies input devices when changed, which is how a runtime `hyprctl keyword` reaches a keyboard.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-in-cell-per-row/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 5. What the dump shows. `hyprctl devices -j` prints the stored rules of each keyboard - rules, model, layout, variant, options - and for each pointer a `scrollFactor` with two decimals (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:765-772, scrollFactor field; Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:785-802, layout and the other stored names). The keyboard object also carries `active_keymap` and `active_layout_index` (the compiled keymap's active layout, named in XKB's words such as `Portuguese (Brazil)`, not the config's `br`), `capsLock` and `numLock` (locked-modifier state, not the `numlock_by_default` option) and `main` (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:793-801, main and the lock fields), which marks the keyboard `switchxkblayout main` acts on, not the primary hardware keyboard: on this host only the input-method virtual keyboard has it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1934-1942, disableAllKeyboards clears main for physical keyboards). The `mice` list holds every pointer, touchpads included, and its `defaultSpeed` is libinput's default, not the configured sensitivity. A pointer's factor is the device block's `scroll_factor` clamped to 0..100 only when that block explicitly sets it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1376-1383, scroll_factor explicitly set), and is otherwise unset, printed as -1.00 (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1379-1383, nullopt branch). The global `input:scroll_factor` (range 0..2, unlike the block's 0..100 clamp) never reaches the printed field (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:290-300, input:scroll_factor is a separate global option), and neither does `input:touchpad:scroll_factor`.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-in-cell-per-row/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:35 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 6. Virtual keyboards. A virtual keyboard (an input method such as fcitx5) is named `hl-virtual-keyboard`, followed, while `misc:name_vk_after_proc` is on (the default), by `-` and the normalised name of its client's binary or `-unknown` (<redacted-shape>.cpp:11-31, hl-virtual-keyboard naming). The config's names are applied to it once at creation; when its client sends a keymap the keyboard marks the keymap overridden (Hyprland-VirtualKeyboard.cpp:36-44, virtual keyboard override flag), and setKeymap then returns early (Hyprland-IKeyboard.cpp:60-64, keymap overridden early return), so the rules the dump prints for it are the creation-time names, not a witness of the keymap in use; its `active_keymap` does name the active layout of the client's keymap.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-in-cell-per-row/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:36 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 7. Names. A device's name is lower-cased with space, newline and comma replaced by `-` (Hyprland-MiscFunctions.cpp:777-789, lower-case name normalizer), an empty result becomes `unknown-device`, and a name already taken by any input device gets a `-1`, `-2` suffix (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:2119-2131, duplicate suffix). A block written with the product name as the kernel reports it (`Razer DeathAdder V2`) never matches: the lookup compares the stored key exactly. The wiki tells the user to copy the name from `hyprctl devices` (wiki-Keywords.md:79, hyprctl devices names) and documents that per-device options overwrite the `input` ones (wiki-Keywords.md:64-70, wiki override rule).

.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-in-cell-per-row/corpus/knowledge/xdg-terminal-selection-r47.md:33 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] config 1. Lists and their order. `make_paths` builds two ordered lists and one path. `IFS=':'` (xdg-terminal-exec:145) then the config sequence (xdg-terminal-exec:148-163): for each of `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}` and `${XDG_CONFIG_DIRS:-/etc/xdg}`, first every lowercased `$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` item as `${dir}/${desktop}-xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:150-152, the lowercasing done once with `tr` at xdg-terminal-exec:1144), then `${dir}/xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:153); after both config dirs, the same pair per `${XDG_DATA_DIRS:-/usr/local/share:/usr/share}` inside an `xdg-terminal-exec/` subdir (xdg-terminal-exec:157-163). The result `XTE__CONFIGS` is read left to right as *decreasing* preference, so the two system entries come last - which is what makes an `/execarg_default` line in the distro list (step 2) a low-priority default. The applications list (xdg-terminal-exec:166-169) is built the other way round, each new `${dir}/applications` prepended to the front (`XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS=${xte__dir%/}/applications/${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS:+:${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS}}`, xdg-terminal-exec:168), so it ends up in *ascending* preference - lowest-priority data dir first. The cache file is `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/xdg-terminal-exec` (xdg-terminal-exec:172-173).
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-in-cell-per-row/corpus/knowledge/xdg-terminal-selection-r47.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 2. List lines. `read_config_paths` reads every list file immediately, in the order of step 1, rather than on demand (`All config files are read immediatelly, rather than on demand, even if it's more IO intensive`, xdg-terminal-exec:353) and pins the locale to `C` by re-invoking itself (xdg-terminal-exec:355-358). A missing file is not an error (xdg-terminal-exec:365). Each line is trimmed by `read -r` and matched by `case`: the five directives `/enable_cache`, `/disable_cache`, `/execarg_compat`, `/execarg_strict` and `/execarg_default:<id>:<arg>` (xdg-terminal-exec:374-421), of which the first two and the first two of the second pair honour only *the first encountered* occurrence via their `*_CONFIGURED` guards (xdg-terminal-exec:376-379); then the entry-ID form `[a-zA-Z0-9_]* | [+-][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)` (xdg-terminal-exec:425). A leading `+` or `-` is cut off as an exclusion marker (xdg-terminal-exec:427-437): `-id` appends to `XTE__EXCLUDED_ENTRY_IDS` (xdg-terminal-exec:462) and `+id` protects an id only from a *later* `-id` (the first of the pair wins; an earlier exclusion stands, fixture `<redacted-shape>`), each list refusing duplicates. Only the first `:` splits the line, ID from action ID (xdg-terminal-exec:435-438); both halves must validate (xdg-terminal-exec:439) or the line is discarded with a message (xdg-terminal-exec:467). A plain line is appended to `XTE__ENTRY_IDS` in file order, which is the explicit preference order (xdg-terminal-exec:442). Comments and empty lines match no arm and are ignored.

.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-line-per-row/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:23 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl | what `hyprctl devices -j` prints for a keyboard and a mouse | step 5 | sourced |
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-line-per-row/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:32 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 3. Per-keyboard lookup. For every keyboard, applyConfigToKeyboard reads six keymap names per device (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1213-1238, applyConfigToKeyboard): for example the kb_layout lookup asks the device first and the global option second (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1226-1231, kb_layout and its siblings). The device value counts only when the user set it; otherwise the global fallback applies (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1115-1123, set-by-user test then global fallback). The block exists when one carries the keyboard's exact normalised name (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1196-1201, deviceConfigExists; the name is the `name` the dump prints), and the STRVAL_EMPTY sentinel reads as the empty string (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1156-1168, STRVAL_EMPTY; its spelling `[[EMPTY]]` lives in a Hyprland header outside these pins). The global defaults are `us` for the layout and empty for the rest (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:271-276, default XKB names). When nothing changed since the last apply, the keyboard is skipped (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1270-1280, did not change). Every `input:kb_*` option re-applies input devices when changed, which is how a runtime `hyprctl keyword` reaches a keyboard.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-line-per-row/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 5. What the dump shows. `hyprctl devices -j` prints the stored rules of each keyboard - rules, model, layout, variant, options - and for each pointer a `scrollFactor` with two decimals (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:765-772, scrollFactor field; Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:785-802, layout and the other stored names). The keyboard object also carries `active_keymap` and `active_layout_index` (the compiled keymap's active layout, named in XKB's words such as `Portuguese (Brazil)`, not the config's `br`), `capsLock` and `numLock` (locked-modifier state, not the `numlock_by_default` option) and `main` (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:793-801, main and the lock fields), which marks the keyboard `switchxkblayout main` acts on, not the primary hardware keyboard: on this host only the input-method virtual keyboard has it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1934-1942, disableAllKeyboards clears main for physical keyboards). The `mice` list holds every pointer, touchpads included, and its `defaultSpeed` is libinput's default, not the configured sensitivity. A pointer's factor is the device block's `scroll_factor` clamped to 0..100 only when that block explicitly sets it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1376-1383, scroll_factor explicitly set), and is otherwise unset, printed as -1.00 (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1379-1383, nullopt branch). The global `input:scroll_factor` (range 0..2, unlike the block's 0..100 clamp) never reaches the printed field (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:290-300, input:scroll_factor is a separate global option), and neither does `input:touchpad:scroll_factor`.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-line-per-row/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:35 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 6. Virtual keyboards. A virtual keyboard (an input method such as fcitx5) is named `hl-virtual-keyboard`, followed, while `misc:name_vk_after_proc` is on (the default), by `-` and the normalised name of its client's binary or `-unknown` (<redacted-shape>.cpp:11-31, hl-virtual-keyboard naming). The config's names are applied to it once at creation; when its client sends a keymap the keyboard marks the keymap overridden (Hyprland-VirtualKeyboard.cpp:36-44, virtual keyboard override flag), and setKeymap then returns early (Hyprland-IKeyboard.cpp:60-64, keymap overridden early return), so the rules the dump prints for it are the creation-time names, not a witness of the keymap in use; its `active_keymap` does name the active layout of the client's keymap.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-line-per-row/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:36 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 7. Names. A device's name is lower-cased with space, newline and comma replaced by `-` (Hyprland-MiscFunctions.cpp:777-789, lower-case name normalizer), an empty result becomes `unknown-device`, and a name already taken by any input device gets a `-1`, `-2` suffix (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:2119-2131, duplicate suffix). A block written with the product name as the kernel reports it (`Razer DeathAdder V2`) never matches: the lookup compares the stored key exactly. The wiki tells the user to copy the name from `hyprctl devices` (wiki-Keywords.md:79, hyprctl devices names) and documents that per-device options overwrite the `input` ones (wiki-Keywords.md:64-70, wiki override rule).

.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-line-per-row/corpus/knowledge/xdg-terminal-selection-r47.md:33 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] config 1. Lists and their order. `make_paths` builds two ordered lists and one path. `IFS=':'` (xdg-terminal-exec:145) then the config sequence (xdg-terminal-exec:148-163): for each of `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}` and `${XDG_CONFIG_DIRS:-/etc/xdg}`, first every lowercased `$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` item as `${dir}/${desktop}-xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:150-152, the lowercasing done once with `tr` at xdg-terminal-exec:1144), then `${dir}/xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:153); after both config dirs, the same pair per `${XDG_DATA_DIRS:-/usr/local/share:/usr/share}` inside an `xdg-terminal-exec/` subdir (xdg-terminal-exec:157-163). The result `XTE__CONFIGS` is read left to right as *decreasing* preference, so the two system entries come last - which is what makes an `/execarg_default` line in the distro list (step 2) a low-priority default. The applications list (xdg-terminal-exec:166-169) is built the other way round, each new `${dir}/applications` prepended to the front (`XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS=${xte__dir%/}/applications/${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS:+:${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS}}`, xdg-terminal-exec:168), so it ends up in *ascending* preference - lowest-priority data dir first. The cache file is `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/xdg-terminal-exec` (xdg-terminal-exec:172-173).
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-comment-line-per-row/corpus/knowledge/xdg-terminal-selection-r47.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 2. List lines. `read_config_paths` reads every list file immediately, in the order of step 1, rather than on demand (`All config files are read immediatelly, rather than on demand, even if it's more IO intensive`, xdg-terminal-exec:353) and pins the locale to `C` by re-invoking itself (xdg-terminal-exec:355-358). A missing file is not an error (xdg-terminal-exec:365). Each line is trimmed by `read -r` and matched by `case`: the five directives `/enable_cache`, `/disable_cache`, `/execarg_compat`, `/execarg_strict` and `/execarg_default:<id>:<arg>` (xdg-terminal-exec:374-421), of which the first two and the first two of the second pair honour only *the first encountered* occurrence via their `*_CONFIGURED` guards (xdg-terminal-exec:376-379); then the entry-ID form `[a-zA-Z0-9_]* | [+-][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)` (xdg-terminal-exec:425). A leading `+` or `-` is cut off as an exclusion marker (xdg-terminal-exec:427-437): `-id` appends to `XTE__EXCLUDED_ENTRY_IDS` (xdg-terminal-exec:462) and `+id` protects an id only from a *later* `-id` (the first of the pair wins; an earlier exclusion stands, fixture `<redacted-shape>`), each list refusing duplicates. Only the first `:` splits the line, ID from action ID (xdg-terminal-exec:435-438); both halves must validate (xdg-terminal-exec:439) or the line is discarded with a message (xdg-terminal-exec:467). A plain line is appended to `XTE__ENTRY_IDS` in file order, which is the explicit preference order (xdg-terminal-exec:442). Comments and empty lines match no arm and are ignored.

.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-delete-missing-cites/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:32 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 3. Per-keyboard lookup. For every keyboard, applyConfigToKeyboard reads six keymap names per device (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1213-1238, applyConfigToKeyboard): for example the kb_layout lookup asks the device first and the global option second (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1226-1231, kb_layout and its siblings). The device value counts only when the user set it; otherwise the global fallback applies (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1115-1123, set-by-user test then global fallback). The block exists when one carries the keyboard's exact normalised name (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1196-1201, deviceConfigExists; the name is the `name` the dump prints), and the STRVAL_EMPTY sentinel reads as the empty string (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1156-1168, STRVAL_EMPTY; its spelling `[[EMPTY]]` lives in a Hyprland header outside these pins). The global defaults are `us` for the layout and empty for the rest (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:271-276, default XKB names). When nothing changed since the last apply, the keyboard is skipped (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1270-1280, did not change). Every `input:kb_*` option re-applies input devices when changed, which is how a runtime `hyprctl keyword` reaches a keyboard.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-delete-missing-cites/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 5. What the dump shows. `hyprctl devices -j` prints the stored rules of each keyboard - rules, model, layout, variant, options - and for each pointer a `scrollFactor` with two decimals (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:765-772, scrollFactor field; Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:785-802, layout and the other stored names). The keyboard object also carries `active_keymap` and `active_layout_index` (the compiled keymap's active layout, named in XKB's words such as `Portuguese (Brazil)`, not the config's `br`), `capsLock` and `numLock` (locked-modifier state, not the `numlock_by_default` option) and `main` (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:793-801, main and the lock fields), which marks the keyboard `switchxkblayout main` acts on, not the primary hardware keyboard: on this host only the input-method virtual keyboard has it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1934-1942, disableAllKeyboards clears main for physical keyboards). The `mice` list holds every pointer, touchpads included, and its `defaultSpeed` is libinput's default, not the configured sensitivity. A pointer's factor is the device block's `scroll_factor` clamped to 0..100 only when that block explicitly sets it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1376-1383, scroll_factor explicitly set), and is otherwise unset, printed as -1.00 (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1379-1383, nullopt branch). The global `input:scroll_factor` (range 0..2, unlike the block's 0..100 clamp) never reaches the printed field (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:290-300, input:scroll_factor is a separate global option), and neither does `input:touchpad:scroll_factor`.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-delete-missing-cites/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:35 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 6. Virtual keyboards. A virtual keyboard (an input method such as fcitx5) is named `hl-virtual-keyboard`, followed, while `misc:name_vk_after_proc` is on (the default), by `-` and the normalised name of its client's binary or `-unknown` (<redacted-shape>.cpp:11-31, hl-virtual-keyboard naming). The config's names are applied to it once at creation; when its client sends a keymap the keyboard marks the keymap overridden (Hyprland-VirtualKeyboard.cpp:36-44, virtual keyboard override flag), and setKeymap then returns early (Hyprland-IKeyboard.cpp:60-64, keymap overridden early return), so the rules the dump prints for it are the creation-time names, not a witness of the keymap in use; its `active_keymap` does name the active layout of the client's keymap.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-delete-missing-cites/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:36 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 7. Names. A device's name is lower-cased with space, newline and comma replaced by `-` (Hyprland-MiscFunctions.cpp:777-789, lower-case name normalizer), an empty result becomes `unknown-device`, and a name already taken by any input device gets a `-1`, `-2` suffix (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:2119-2131, duplicate suffix). A block written with the product name as the kernel reports it (`Razer DeathAdder V2`) never matches: the lookup compares the stored key exactly. .ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-delete-missing-cites/corpus/knowledge/xdg-terminal-selection-r47.md:33 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] config 1. Lists and their order. `make_paths` builds two ordered lists and one path. `IFS=':'` (xdg-terminal-exec:145) then the config sequence (xdg-terminal-exec:148-163): for each of `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}` and `${XDG_CONFIG_DIRS:-/etc/xdg}`, first every lowercased `$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` item as `${dir}/${desktop}-xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:150-152, the lowercasing done once with `tr` at xdg-terminal-exec:1144), then `${dir}/xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:153); after both config dirs, the same pair per `${XDG_DATA_DIRS:-/usr/local/share:/usr/share}` inside an `xdg-terminal-exec/` subdir (xdg-terminal-exec:157-163). The result `XTE__CONFIGS` is read left to right as *decreasing* preference, so the two system entries come last - which is what makes an `/execarg_default` line in the distro list (step 2) a low-priority default. The applications list (xdg-terminal-exec:166-169) is built the other way round, each new `${dir}/applications` prepended to the front (`XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS=${xte__dir%/}/applications/${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS:+:${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS}}`, xdg-terminal-exec:168), so it ends up in *ascending* preference - lowest-priority data dir first. The cache file is `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/xdg-terminal-exec` (xdg-terminal-exec:172-173).
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-delete-missing-cites/corpus/knowledge/xdg-terminal-selection-r47.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 2. List lines. `read_config_paths` reads every list file immediately, in the order of step 1, rather than on demand (`All config files are read immediatelly, rather than on demand, even if it's more IO intensive`, xdg-terminal-exec:353) and pins the locale to `C` by re-invoking itself (xdg-terminal-exec:355-358). A missing file is not an error (xdg-terminal-exec:365). Each line is trimmed by `read -r` and matched by `case`: the five directives `/enable_cache`, `/disable_cache`, `/execarg_compat`, `/execarg_strict` and `/execarg_default:<id>:<arg>` (xdg-terminal-exec:374-421), of which the first two and the first two of the second pair honour only *the first encountered* occurrence via their `*_CONFIGURED` guards (xdg-terminal-exec:376-379); then the entry-ID form `[a-zA-Z0-9_]* | [+-][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)` (xdg-terminal-exec:425). A leading `+` or `-` is cut off as an exclusion marker (xdg-terminal-exec:427-437): `-id` appends to `XTE__EXCLUDED_ENTRY_IDS` (xdg-terminal-exec:462) and `+id` protects an id only from a *later* `-id` (the first of the pair wins; an earlier exclusion stands, fixture `<redacted-shape>`), each list refusing duplicates. Only the first `:` splits the line, ID from action ID (xdg-terminal-exec:435-438); both halves must validate (xdg-terminal-exec:439) or the line is discarded with a message (xdg-terminal-exec:467). A plain line is appended to `XTE__ENTRY_IDS` in file order, which is the explicit preference order (xdg-terminal-exec:442). Comments and empty lines match no arm and are ignored.

.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-fill-all/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:32 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 3. Per-keyboard lookup. For every keyboard, applyConfigToKeyboard reads six keymap names per device (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1213-1238, applyConfigToKeyboard): for example the kb_layout lookup asks the device first and the global option second (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1226-1231, kb_layout and its siblings). The device value counts only when the user set it; otherwise the global fallback applies (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1115-1123, set-by-user test then global fallback). The block exists when one carries the keyboard's exact normalised name (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1196-1201, deviceConfigExists; the name is the `name` the dump prints), and the STRVAL_EMPTY sentinel reads as the empty string (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1156-1168, STRVAL_EMPTY; its spelling `[[EMPTY]]` lives in a Hyprland header outside these pins). The global defaults are `us` for the layout and empty for the rest (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:271-276, default XKB names). When nothing changed since the last apply, the keyboard is skipped (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1270-1280, did not change). Every `input:kb_*` option re-applies input devices when changed, which is how a runtime `hyprctl keyword` reaches a keyboard.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-fill-all/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 5. What the dump shows. `hyprctl devices -j` prints the stored rules of each keyboard - rules, model, layout, variant, options - and for each pointer a `scrollFactor` with two decimals (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:765-772, scrollFactor field; Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:785-802, layout and the other stored names). The keyboard object also carries `active_keymap` and `active_layout_index` (the compiled keymap's active layout, named in XKB's words such as `Portuguese (Brazil)`, not the config's `br`), `capsLock` and `numLock` (locked-modifier state, not the `numlock_by_default` option) and `main` (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:793-801, main and the lock fields), which marks the keyboard `switchxkblayout main` acts on, not the primary hardware keyboard: on this host only the input-method virtual keyboard has it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1934-1942, disableAllKeyboards clears main for physical keyboards). The `mice` list holds every pointer, touchpads included, and its `defaultSpeed` is libinput's default, not the configured sensitivity. A pointer's factor is the device block's `scroll_factor` clamped to 0..100 only when that block explicitly sets it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1376-1383, scroll_factor explicitly set), and is otherwise unset, printed as -1.00 (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1379-1383, nullopt branch). The global `input:scroll_factor` (range 0..2, unlike the block's 0..100 clamp) never reaches the printed field (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:290-300, input:scroll_factor is a separate global option), and neither does `input:touchpad:scroll_factor`.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-fill-all/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:35 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 6. Virtual keyboards. A virtual keyboard (an input method such as fcitx5) is named `hl-virtual-keyboard`, followed, while `misc:name_vk_after_proc` is on (the default), by `-` and the normalised name of its client's binary or `-unknown` (<redacted-shape>.cpp:11-31, hl-virtual-keyboard naming). The config's names are applied to it once at creation; when its client sends a keymap the keyboard marks the keymap overridden (Hyprland-VirtualKeyboard.cpp:36-44, virtual keyboard override flag), and setKeymap then returns early (Hyprland-IKeyboard.cpp:60-64, keymap overridden early return), so the rules the dump prints for it are the creation-time names, not a witness of the keymap in use; its `active_keymap` does name the active layout of the client's keymap.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-fill-all/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:36 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 7. Names. A device's name is lower-cased with space, newline and comma replaced by `-` (Hyprland-MiscFunctions.cpp:777-789, lower-case name normalizer), an empty result becomes `unknown-device`, and a name already taken by any input device gets a `-1`, `-2` suffix (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:2119-2131, duplicate suffix). A block written with the product name as the kernel reports it (`Razer DeathAdder V2`) never matches: the lookup compares the stored key exactly. The wiki tells the user to copy the name from `hyprctl devices` (wiki-Keywords.md:79, hyprctl devices names) and documents that per-device options overwrite the `input` ones (wiki-Keywords.md:64-70, wiki override rule).

Lists and their order. `make_paths` builds two ordered lists and one path. `IFS=':'` (xdg-terminal-exec:145) then the config sequence (xdg-terminal-exec:148-163): for each of `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}` and `${XDG_CONFIG_DIRS:-/etc/xdg}`, first every lowercased `$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` item as `${dir}/${desktop}-xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:150-152, the lowercasing done once with `tr` at xdg-terminal-exec:1144), then `${dir}/xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:153); after both config dirs, the same pair per `${XDG_DATA_DIRS:-/usr/local/share:/usr/share}` inside an `xdg-terminal-exec/` subdir (xdg-terminal-exec:157-163). The result `XTE__CONFIGS` is read left to right as *decreasing* preference, so the two system entries come last - which is what makes an `/execarg_default` line in the distro list (step 2) a low-priority default. The applications list (xdg-terminal-exec:166-169) is built the other way round, each new `${dir}/applications` prepended to the front (`XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS=${xte__dir%/}/applications/${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS:+:${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS}}`, xdg-terminal-exec:168), so it ends up in *ascending* preference - lowest-priority data dir first. The cache file is `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/xdg-terminal-exec` (xdg-terminal-exec:172-173).

List lines. `read_config_paths` reads every list file immediately, in the order of step 1, rather than on demand (`All config files are read immediatelly, rather than on demand, even if it's more IO intensive`, xdg-terminal-exec:353) and pins the locale to `C` by re-invoking itself (xdg-terminal-exec:355-358). Only the first `:` splits the line, ID from action ID (xdg-terminal-exec:435-438); both halves must validate (xdg-terminal-exec:439) or the line is discarded with a message (xdg-terminal-exec:467). A plain line is appended to `XTE__ENTRY_IDS` in file order, which is the explicit preference order (xdg-terminal-exec:442). Comments and empty lines match no arm and are ignored.

.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-strip-all-citations/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:23 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl | what `hyprctl devices -j` prints for a keyboard and a mouse | step 5 | sourced |
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-strip-all-citations/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:32 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 3. Per-keyboard lookup. For every keyboard, applyConfigToKeyboard reads six keymap names per device (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1213-1238, applyConfigToKeyboard): for example the kb_layout lookup asks the device first and the global option second (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1226-1231, kb_layout and its siblings). The device value counts only when the user set it; otherwise the global fallback applies (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1115-1123, set-by-user test then global fallback). The block exists when one carries the keyboard's exact normalised name (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1196-1201, deviceConfigExists; the name is the `name` the dump prints), and the STRVAL_EMPTY sentinel reads as the empty string (Hyprland-ConfigManager.cpp:1156-1168, STRVAL_EMPTY; its spelling `[[EMPTY]]` lives in a Hyprland header outside these pins). The global defaults are `us` for the layout and empty for the rest (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:271-276, default XKB names). When nothing changed since the last apply, the keyboard is skipped (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1270-1280, did not change). Every `input:kb_*` option re-applies input devices when changed, which is how a runtime `hyprctl keyword` reaches a keyboard.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-strip-all-citations/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 5. What the dump shows. `hyprctl devices -j` prints the stored rules of each keyboard - rules, model, layout, variant, options - and for each pointer a `scrollFactor` with two decimals (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:765-772, scrollFactor field; Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:785-802, layout and the other stored names). The keyboard object also carries `active_keymap` and `active_layout_index` (the compiled keymap's active layout, named in XKB's words such as `Portuguese (Brazil)`, not the config's `br`), `capsLock` and `numLock` (locked-modifier state, not the `numlock_by_default` option) and `main` (Hyprland-HyprCtl.cpp:793-801, main and the lock fields), which marks the keyboard `switchxkblayout main` acts on, not the primary hardware keyboard: on this host only the input-method virtual keyboard has it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1934-1942, disableAllKeyboards clears main for physical keyboards). The `mice` list holds every pointer, touchpads included, and its `defaultSpeed` is libinput's default, not the configured sensitivity. A pointer's factor is the device block's `scroll_factor` clamped to 0..100 only when that block explicitly sets it (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1376-1383, scroll_factor explicitly set), and is otherwise unset, printed as -1.00 (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:1379-1383, nullopt branch). The global `input:scroll_factor` (range 0..2, unlike the block's 0..100 clamp) never reaches the printed field (Hyprland-ConfigValues.cpp:290-300, input:scroll_factor is a separate global option), and neither does `input:touchpad:scroll_factor`.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-strip-all-citations/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:35 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 6. Virtual keyboards. A virtual keyboard (an input method such as fcitx5) is named `hl-virtual-keyboard`, followed, while `misc:name_vk_after_proc` is on (the default), by `-` and the normalised name of its client's binary or `-unknown` (<redacted-shape>.cpp:11-31, hl-virtual-keyboard naming). The config's names are applied to it once at creation; when its client sends a keymap the keyboard marks the keymap overridden (Hyprland-VirtualKeyboard.cpp:36-44, virtual keyboard override flag), and setKeymap then returns early (Hyprland-IKeyboard.cpp:60-64, keymap overridden early return), so the rules the dump prints for it are the creation-time names, not a witness of the keymap in use; its `active_keymap` does name the active layout of the client's keymap.
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-strip-all-citations/corpus/knowledge/hyprland-input-devices-r46.md:36 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl 7. Names. A device's name is lower-cased with space, newline and comma replaced by `-` (Hyprland-MiscFunctions.cpp:777-789, lower-case name normalizer), an empty result becomes `unknown-device`, and a name already taken by any input device gets a `-1`, `-2` suffix (Hyprland-InputManager.cpp:2119-2131, duplicate suffix). A block written with the product name as the kernel reports it (`Razer DeathAdder V2`) never matches: the lookup compares the stored key exactly. The wiki tells the user to copy the name from `hyprctl devices` (wiki-Keywords.md:79, hyprctl devices names) and documents that per-device options overwrite the `input` ones (wiki-Keywords.md:64-70, wiki override rule).

.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-strip-all-citations/corpus/knowledge/xdg-terminal-selection-r47.md:33 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] config 1. Lists and their order. `make_paths` builds two ordered lists and one path. `IFS=':'` (xdg-terminal-exec:145) then the config sequence (xdg-terminal-exec:148-163): for each of `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}` and `${XDG_CONFIG_DIRS:-/etc/xdg}`, first every lowercased `$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` item as `${dir}/${desktop}-xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:150-152, the lowercasing done once with `tr` at xdg-terminal-exec:1144), then `${dir}/xdg-terminals.list` (xdg-terminal-exec:153); after both config dirs, the same pair per `${XDG_DATA_DIRS:-/usr/local/share:/usr/share}` inside an `xdg-terminal-exec/` subdir (xdg-terminal-exec:157-163). The result `XTE__CONFIGS` is read left to right as *decreasing* preference, so the two system entries come last - which is what makes an `/execarg_default` line in the distro list (step 2) a low-priority default. The applications list (xdg-terminal-exec:166-169) is built the other way round, each new `${dir}/applications` prepended to the front (`XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS=${xte__dir%/}/applications/${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS:+:${XTE__APPLICATIONS_DIRS}}`, xdg-terminal-exec:168), so it ends up in *ascending* preference - lowest-priority data dir first. The cache file is `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/xdg-terminal-exec` (xdg-terminal-exec:172-173).
.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-strip-all-citations/corpus/knowledge/xdg-terminal-selection-r47.md:34 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] fixed3 2. List lines. `read_config_paths` reads every list file immediately, in the order of step 1, rather than on demand (`All config files are read immediatelly, rather than on demand, even if it's more IO intensive`, xdg-terminal-exec:353) and pins the locale to `C` by re-invoking itself (xdg-terminal-exec:355-358). A missing file is not an error (xdg-terminal-exec:365). Each line is trimmed by `read -r` and matched by `case`: the five directives `/enable_cache`, `/disable_cache`, `/execarg_compat`, `/execarg_strict` and `/execarg_default:<id>:<arg>` (xdg-terminal-exec:374-421), of which the first two and the first two of the second pair honour only *the first encountered* occurrence via their `*_CONFIGURED` guards (xdg-terminal-exec:376-379); then the entry-ID form `[a-zA-Z0-9_]* | [+-][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)` (xdg-terminal-exec:425). A leading `+` or `-` is cut off as an exclusion marker (xdg-terminal-exec:427-437): `-id` appends to `XTE__EXCLUDED_ENTRY_IDS` (xdg-terminal-exec:462) and `+id` protects an id only from a *later* `-id` (the first of the pair wins; an earlier exclusion stands, fixture `<redacted-shape>`), each list refusing duplicates. Only the first `:` splits the line, ID from action ID (xdg-terminal-exec:435-438); both halves must validate (xdg-terminal-exec:439) or the line is discarded with a message (xdg-terminal-exec:467). A plain line is appended to `XTE__ENTRY_IDS` in file order, which is the explicit preference order (xdg-terminal-exec:442). Comments and empty lines match no arm and are ignored.

.ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56CritDoNothing/receipts/artifacts/c3-strip-all-citations/corpus/knowledge/xkb-keymap-compile-r48.md:41 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] config 6. **File and map lookup.** The generated component names are resolved as `symbols/<file>` over the include paths, first hit wins over the ordered list (xkbcommon-include.c:333); the order is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/xkb` (else `$HOME/.config/xkb`), `$HOME/.xkb`, `$XKB_CONFIG_EXTRA_PATH` (`/etc/xkb`), the versioned then unversioned extension directories, and `$XKB_CONFIG_ROOT` (`/usr/share/xkeyboard-config-2`) last (xkbcommon-context.c:243-338). A required file that no path has logs XKB-338 with a census of the paths searched and the paths that could not be added (xkbcommon-include.c:353-358); a file that exists but carries no map of that name logs XKB-661 with the include statement (xkbcommon-include.c:498-506). If the configured root cannot be appended, the legacy root `/usr/share/X11/xkb` is tried instead, silently at the default log level (xkbcommon-context.c:327-337). .ufo/waves/round-56/w1/R56ScribeIndex/03-PROVINCE-refinement.md:5 [NO_DEFECT_CANDIDATE_DATA] hyprctl **Round-56 refinement (append-only; one read-only tool, three record instruments, one knowledge entry; no new write surface):** `tools/mado-watchplan.py` is a read-only join. It reads only the files its caller names: `--config` (the main Hyprland config, a regular file), at most one `--getoption` file (a captured `hyprctl getoption misc:disable_autoreload -j` reply, 1 MiB cap), and the files that the config's `source =` lines reach (absolute, `~` with `--home`, relative and glob forms); on those paths it calls only `stat`, `lstat`, `realpath`, `glob` and the `isdir`, `lexists` and `islink` checks. From these it predicts the inotify watch list Hyprland 0.56.2 registers for the config tree and reads `misc:disable_autoreload` the way hyprlang does. Constructs outside its model are counted `unsupported` and never guessed. It starts no process, opens no socket and writes nothing; the operator captures the `getoption` reply with the read verb and applies no change. Its capability row enters SCORECARD only on the round's C2 `TARGET_MET`. The record instruments are `quality/counters/c1-r56-autoreload-entry.py` (the entry's counter), `quality/counters/c3-r56-used-by.py` (the registry used-by counter) and `quality/check-r56-controls.py` (the independent harness). The two counters read git objects only, at the revision they are given, and write nothing. The harness also reads git objects, but it builds scratch repositories, exports the tool and its fixtures and runs them and the counters as child processes, writing only under its `--work` directory; it never writes the lane or the fleet repo. None of them touches a config plane, the compositor, a socket or a host service. Reload, inotify delivery and the Lua config provider stay outside every instrument.
